title: Insertion of Flexible Neural Probes Using Rigid Stiffeners Attached with Biodissolvable Adhesive
protocol: Assemble a silicon stiffener using standard microfabrication processes.
Fabricate a thin-film polymer probe.
Attach the polymer probe to the silicon stiffener.
Use a shallow "wicking" channel on the stiffener to distribute liquid adhesive during assembly.
Handle the wider tab portion of the stiffener for ease during assembly and surgical insertion.
Dry-etch wicking channels using the standard Bosch process on a silicon-on-insulator (SOI) wafer.
Etch stiffener geometry to stop on the buried oxide layer.
Release stiffeners by wet-etching the buried oxide layer in 49% hydrofluoric acid.
Thoroughly rinse stiffeners with deionized water.
Soak stiffeners in deionized water for 15 min.
Place a pellet of polyethylene glycol (PEG) of molecular weight 10,000 g/mol into the reservoir.
Heat stiffener to 65 °C until PEG melts and wicks into the channel by capillary action.
Cool stiffener to room temperature to solidify PEG.
Place stiffener upside down on base stage of flip chip bonder.
Pick up stiffener with tool head.
Place probe upside down on base stage.
Align stiffener and probe using flip chip bonder.
Lower stiffener onto probe.
Heat the base stage of the flip chip bonder to apply heat to the substrate.
Place the stiffener on the heated substrate.
Heat the assembly to 65 °C.
Allow one minute for the PEG to remelt and fill in the interface between the probe and stiffener.
Cool the assembly to solidify the PEG.
Turn the assembly over and inspect from the top.
Reheat as needed to ensure the PEG completely fills the interface between the probe and stiffener.
Manually place 1-3 extra pellets of solid PEG onto the tab.
Allow the assembly to cool until the PEG solidifies.
Prepare the assembly for surgical insertion.
Mount the probe-stiffener assembly to a micromanipulator at the tab region.
Adhere the back of the stiffener to the micromanipulator arm with double-sided tape or cement, avoiding contact between the adhesive and the probe.
Secure the connector end of the probe to the micromanipulator with a small piece of adhesive putty for easy removal.
Position the probe assembly over the target site.
Insert the probe into the target at an insertion speed of 0.13-0.5 mm/sec.
Gently remove the connector end of the probe from the micromanipulator and rest it on a nearby surface.
Allow time for PEG to dissolve, which may take approximately 15 minutes depending on PEG molecular weight and contact area.
Apply phosphate buffered saline (PBS) around the tab and insertion point using a dropper to dissolve any remaining PEG above the target.
Prepare a solution of 0.6% agarose in phosphate buffered saline (PBS) by heating until completely dissolved.
Pour the agarose-PBS solution into a shallow acrylic box, ensuring the gel is 3/4-1 inch deep.
Allow the gel to set at room temperature for an hour.
Saturate the hardened gel with PBS to prevent drying.
Heat the gel to 37 °C.
Set up the micromanipulator, box of agarose gel, and microscopic camera system.
Insert a glass reference fiducial into the box of gel by sliding it between the gel and the side of the box.
Square the features on the reference fiducial using a dental pick to align them with the field of view of the digital microscope.
Mount the probe assembly to the micromanipulator as described in step 2.1.
Position the probe assembly over the gel about 1 mm behind the reference fiducial.
Insert the probe into the gel, guided by the camera to a desired depth in the field of view.
Move the connector end of the probe to rest on a nearby surface immediately after insertion.
Adjust the camera image to focus on the probe if necessary (the reference fiducial features may be slightly out of focus).
Take a snapshot of the probe location.
Allow PEG to dissolve (this time may vary, and in fact may be a parameter to be tested).
Apply PBS near the tab to dissolve PEG that is above the gel.
Start video capture if desired.
Begin extraction of the stiffener as described in step 2.5.
Take a final snapshot of probe location when extraction is complete.
Use image processing tools to compare the images before and after stiffener extraction.
Register (align) the images using the features on the reference fiducial that are visible in the field of view.
Calibrate the scale of the image based on the size of known features on the probe.
Measure the distance of probe displacement.
